primitives.name: Orinq receipts pallet
primitives.desc: Receipt registry with M-of-N committee attestation that counts and pays only current committee members and clamps the threshold to the committee on every removal, availability certification, anchor records, attestor bonds and slashing, and fee escrow — the on-chain truth every other primitive commits to. Root names backup signers, committee members whose attestations count toward the threshold unpaid and are refused until a set number of blocks after the receipt's submission: they earn no emission reward, and their fee shares are burned, so the members that sign first are the ones paid, a submitter pays the whole fee whoever signs, and certification never waits on them alone. The delay stays under half of the receipt expiry window. Benchmarked threshold and non-threshold attestation paths return actual weights; conditional Currency calls refund unused MOTRA checkpoint budgets. Every refunded Currency base is pinned to maximum Wasm samples and independent storage proofs, including zero-balance branches. Non-threshold, duplicate backstop and departed-signer weights depend on the signers each attest decodes and cover each measured signer-count median with an upward-adjusted FRAME fit, including the complete duty pre/dispatch/post path. Pure Utility attestation batches fill the block at each attestation's actual storage-priced weight; invalid and non-canonical duty calls are rejected before payment; a pure batch may carry no more stale attests than new ones. Block hooks price the storage they read and write, and runtime upgrades keep attestations in flight. A genesis may fix the chain's MATRA issuance: the era emission then mints nothing; the receipt fee, the bond requirement and the attestation reward are stored as zero and Root can set no other, since each makes a certification or a slash move, mint or burn MATRA; the runtime's genesis builder refuses a genesis whose declared issuance differs from what it issues, the Treasury's existential deposit included; and try-runtime holds Balances.TotalIssuance to it. A genesis may also seat the attestation committee and its threshold, so receipts certify from block one: each member listed once and holding a provider, the threshold from 1 to the committee's size; a genesis that seats none stores neither item. The era's books (authored blocks, start block, per-era attestation counters and the era event) roll over every era whether or not it minted.

primitives.name: MOTRA fee resource
primitives.desc: Non-transferable transaction-fee resource generated from the lowest free MATRA held throughout each checkpoint interval (NIGHT/DUST model), with balance-change checkpoints preventing backdated funding and cycling, PalletId sovereign generation excluded, and a constant-cost legacy migration with an upgrade-block earning baseline. Gemtek Wasm benchmarks price checkpoint storage per touched account; runtime dispatch weights and initialization budgets cover Currency callers and batched transfers, with storage-observation property tests; settlement weights generated on this runtime already carry their checkpoints, so the runtime adds none to them. Account creation does not write MOTRA state. Charged by a signed extension, with sponsor delegation for fresh accounts' first fees; the extension also gives a runtime-named (signer, call) set the top transaction-pool priority, one slot per signer, so the guardian's veto cannot be outbid for a place in a block. Retention and generated credit use bounded logarithmic conservative decay; the complete fee extension is benchmarked and refunds unused actual weight using the paid price. Committed Wasm samples pin checkpoint, reconciliation and fee weights. Signed-base and call work are both congestion priced; paid priority uses only the non-refundable base. Canonical new committee attests and pure Utility batches are feeless duties with signer/receipt replay tags and pre-dispatch revalidation; the guardian retains highest priority. Refunds preserve the signed base and max_balance, including arithmetic saturation. Paid Operational-class calls are refused before payment unless the guardian's veto takes them first or the runtime names the signer's path (sudo key's exempt calls, ready timelock enactment, authorized upgrades, settlement committee and bounded keeper calls); a decode sweep pins every Operational call and wrapper. Congestion meters Normal plus Operational weight against the Normal budget, excluding Mandatory weight and the guardian's veto. Receipt submissions prepay their committee's feeless certification work at R. Storage is priced at the runtime's RocksDB DbWeight, and one call may declare its class budget less a 1% initialization reservation.

primitives.name: Billing pallet
primitives.desc: Application-layer MATRA billing (pay_request) for API calls, metering and attestation evidence — the user-facing spend surface, distinct from MOTRA tx fees. Topups and withdrawals use measured Wasm execution and storage-proof bounds while refunding unused MOTRA checkpoint surcharges.

primitives.name: TEE attestation pallet
primitives.desc: Hardware attestation-evidence registry: verifies Android key-attestation chains (Google attestation roots only, attestation extension in the leaf only, TEE or StrongBox keys) and records one against a receipt only when the leaf challenge is SHA-256 of a domain tag, the chain genesis hash, the receipt id and the content hash OrinqReceipts holds for it, so evidence cannot be replayed onto another receipt or network; certificates above the leaf must be outside a Root-maintained revocation set (serials passed as hex text exactly as Google's status list writes them, canonicalized on chain) and valid at the block timestamp, expired factory-provisioned intermediates excepted as Google's verifier does; only the receipt's submitter or a receipt-committee member may attach evidence, one entry per evidence type, checked before any signature work; submit_evidence is priced at its measured Wasm worst case (five P-384 signature checks); a versioned migration clears evidence recorded before binding; a per-receipt composite trust score feeds certification. Disabled at genesis behind a Root kill-switch.

primitives.name: Committee seating gate
primitives.desc: Composed authority-selection gate: input sanitizer, dead-registered and dead-core liveness filters, seat-ramp clamp, live-quorum floor, growth-slack invariant, break-glass floor and pinned-committee override; refuses (keep-current) rather than seat a committee that cannot finalize, so a fresh chain keeps the genesis committee its chain spec declares until a quorum of Cardano's draw has authored. The author and every importing peer judge it on the same state: the runtime's check_inherents initialises the block first. Genesis refuses a chain spec whose committee is empty, has Aura or GRANDPA authorities seeded beside it, has more seats than MaxValidators, lists an authority twice or out of ascending cross-chain-key order, or gives two authorities one Aura or GRANDPA key. A raw chain spec never runs that builder, so the node refuses to load any spec whose genesis committee is empty or whose genesis Aura or GRANDPA authorities are not the committee's keys in its order, naming the reason; preprod v6, which started before the live-quorum floor and seated Cardano's draw at its first rotation, is the one genesis it loads despite that.

primitives.name: Main-chain follower
primitives.desc: Cardano main-chain follower backends (db-sync and yaci-store with Mithril-certified stake) supplying candidate registrations and the D-parameter to authority selection. Like upstream partner-chains, both serve the committee for a Cardano epoch from the data of the epoch two before it. CI checks the db-sync lag on an isolated Postgres and requires its sources to match upstream v1.5.1. Preprod v6, keyed by the genesis hash read once from the node's client, draws every committee under the relaxation it has always run, from the data of the Cardano epoch each session starts in.

primitives.name: Mainnet launch preflight
primitives.desc: Fail-closed genesis and launch gate: reads the raw chain spec, the runtime metadata extracted from its code, the authority launch commands (opening sh -c wrappers) and each authority's running node argv from a /proc/<pid>/cmdline capture, the nginx and cloudflared RPC proxy configs, each public RPC URL probed live over HTTP and a WebSocket, and Cardano mainnet through Kupo (the cMATRA genesis lock and its datum, and the permissioned candidates datum). Refuses on a well-known key anywhere (genesis, runtime code, any role or multisig member, the Cardano committee, node configs including dev-phrase URIs and the dev seed, the signing key), the table holding published secrets and keys whose secret anyone can name (k·B and k·G for every scalar k up to 1024, and the keys of the all-0x00, all-0x01 and all-0xff mini-secrets), found in one pass over each blob's 8-byte blocks whatever the table's size; a key whose signature of any message needs no secret (the all-zero sr25519 key, or any of the 14 ed25519 small-order encodings ed25519-zebra accepts, enumerated from the curve) in any role or multisig member, or as an aura or grandpa key in genesis Aura.Authorities, Grandpa.Authorities, SessionCommitteeManagement.CurrentCommittee or Session.ValidatorsAndKeys, a declared authority or a Cardano permissioned candidate; Sudo.Key, the attestation committee or its threshold other than roles.attestors and attestation_threshold, a 33-byte role key that is no compressed ECDSA key, or a genesis account no declared role or the Treasury accounts for, Root not a multisig two keyholders must sign for (one key that meets its threshold alone through a nested multisig, or with the keys anyone can sign as, counts as one keyholder, and a multisig those keys meet alone as anyone's) or one with a multisig at any depth of more members than the runtime's Multisig.MaxSignatories, which pallet_multisig never signs through, an undeclared off-chain role, a chain spec the anchor worker would read as a test network, attestor or validator reward parameters that are undeclared or not what genesis and the runtime hold, unsafe RPC on an authority, a public RPC URL that lists a method outside the safe set or answers an unsafe one, an authority with no launch entry, genesis storage outside an allowlist (settlement's own storage version, closed legacy cutovers, Cardano ids, the fixed issuance and the attestation committee are on it), a genesis that does not fix its MATRA issuance or fixes another than its accounts hold and the launch's dust plus the Treasury's existential deposit sum to, one MATRA or more, an account holding other than its declared dust, a non-zero attestation reward, receipt fee, fee floor or bond, issuance above what the genesis lock holds, a lock fewer than two key holders can spend or not bound to this genesis, PerpEngine under any name, a runtime override or code substitute, a LastRuntimeUpgrade other than the spec version and name build-spec writes for the genesis code, a genesis-enabled Cardano deposit observation with no checkpoint, genesis, code, chain-spec and launch manifest hashes that differ from a manifest signed by a launch key the repo pins, a Root timelock guardian missing from genesis, not the declared multisig, not needing two keyholders or over MaxSignatories by the same test as Root, with a nested multisig member (whose veto the runtime does not take first), the sudo key or sharing any account or member with it, or timelock delays missing, below the runtime's mainnet delays, above its MaxDelay or out of order, both read from the runtime metadata; and a member of a multisig, in any role at any depth, that does not prove possession of its key: a bare key, the all-zero key, no pop, or a pop that is not its key's sr25519 (ECDSA for a 33-byte key) signature of a challenge binding a domain, the chain spec's name and id, the genesis hash, the launch manifest hash taken without the pops, its role and its position, which the challenge subcommand prints for its holder to sign offline with subkey sign --hex; and hex in the raw spec, the manifests, the launch keys or the key tables in any spelling but the one its writer writes, or a JSON object in them that names a key twice, since the node reads another spelling as other bytes; and a number genesis stores (an attestor reward, the bond, the issuance, an account) at any width but its type's, or an account under any key but its own, which the node reads as zero or never reads; and an authority whose own node binary, pinned by sha256 and captured from its running process, run offline through export-blocks on its running argv's chain and database options, builds another genesis than the one the preflight computes, so any reading of the spec the preflight gets apart from the node shows as another hash, whose --chain names a chain built into the node or a file that is not the checked spec, or that runs another binary than the manifest pins; an authority whose running node serves another genesis as block 0 (its chain_getBlockHash 0, captured from its local RPC), as a node started on a database that already held one or on a spec file overwritten since does, or names another chain, chain type or properties than the checked spec (system_chain, system_chainType and system_properties), or whose --chain path (each directory on it and the file, by the ctime stat prints, against the process start /proc/<pid>/stat and /proc/stat give) changed less than a second before its node process started, since a node keeps the spec it read at its start; and an authority launch that runs a node subcommand other than build-spec or purge-chain before its node, since the others write a genesis into the base path; and a genesis committee (SessionCommitteeManagement.CurrentCommittee, which the runtime seats at every rotation whose Cardano draw fails, a fresh chain's first among them) that is not exactly the declared authorities' aura and grandpa key pairs, each once, is longer than the runtime's MaxValidators or serves an epoch other than 0, genesis Aura and GRANDPA authorities other than the declared keys, each once and every voter at weight 1, a genesis Grandpa.CurrentSetId other than 0 or a Grandpa.SetIdSession other than build-spec's set 0 in session 0, since a warp-synced node takes the runtime's set id, session validators other than the committee as the session genesis writes it, a filled pallet_session stub, two authorities that declare one key, a list length in more bytes than parity-scale-codec accepts, or a Cardano permissioned candidate's gran key other than the grandpa key the authority with its aura key declares, or a declared authority on no candidate, which the first committee drawn from Cardano leaves out; and genesis committee scripts whose candidate address is past the runtime's 120-byte MainchainAddress, which the runtime reads as all-zero policies, or is not UTF-8 or holds a NUL byte, which the node's follower panics on or cannot query; and a permissioned candidates datum (read, with the D-parameter, from the one unspent output holding each policy's token, in the formats the node's partner-chains v1.5.1 follower decodes) that holds a candidate Ariadne drops, repeats a key, or holds fewer than the two candidates the runtime draws a committee from, or a D-parameter that seats registered candidates, fewer permissioned seats than candidates, or more than MaxValidators; and a genesis Sidechain.SlotsPerEpoch other than the launch's declared slots_per_epoch, 0 (every block's initialization divides by it), or one whose sessions do not divide Cardano's epoch, as partner-chains' sidechain-slots requires; and an authority whose Cardano follower settings (the MC__ epoch layout, CARDANO_SECURITY_PARAMETER and CARDANO_ACTIVE_SLOTS_COEFF, from its env or anywhere in its launch) are missing or not, string for string, the launch's declared cardano_follower, or a declared set other than Cardano mainnet's, since a node on other settings than its peers' draws another committee or judges another Cardano block stable and refuses their committee changes and blocks. It also runs each pinned node binary's chain-id on the checked spec, which reads the spec runtime's metadata once block one has initialised on the genesis, and refuses a chain id there (any constant named ChainId or GenesisHash) other than the genesis hash, which would fail every signature the chain's committee and attestors make, or other Cardano ids read from the spec than the preflight reads. It refuses a genesis IntentSettlement.CardanoIds, the Cardano network every voucher digest and evidence check binds, that is absent, holds another network magic or Shelley genesis hash than Cardano mainnet's published ones, or an Aegis policy hash other than the one the launch manifest declares, or any where the manifest declares the policy bound after genesis (null), since a policy applied to the chain's own genesis hash can only be bound after it. It reads the node's mainnet manifest fields (dust, attestation_threshold, partner_chain, each authority's cross_chain, and the roles the builder knows, refusing any other field or role), refuses a genesis committee member or Cardano candidate under another partner-chain key than its authority declares, derives the committee candidate address and the D-parameter and permissioned candidates policy ids from the genesis UTXO as partner-chains v1.8.0 does (the vendored v8.1.0 raw scripts applied as Plutus data by its own flat encoder, hashed as Plutus V2) and refuses a manifest or genesis naming others, refuses committee datum outputs created within two Cardano epochs of the launch and names the earliest valid launch, and refuses any role signer without a provider or below the existential deposit plus the multisig and recovery deposits its roles reserve, from the runtime's constants. Its well-known keys include every retired preprod key (exposed_keys.json), and check requires the operator's table of exposed keys.

primitives.name: Mainnet chain-spec builder
primitives.desc: materios-node build-spec --chain mainnet:<launch manifest> builds the mainnet genesis from the launch manifest the launch preflight reads, extended with dust (role -> account -> base units), attestation_threshold, partner_chain (genesis UTXO, committee candidate address, D-parameter and permissioned candidates policy ids) and each authority's partner-chain key. Genesis fixes MATRA's issuance at the sum of the dust plus the Treasury's existential deposit, under one MATRA, with zero attestation reward, fee, floor and bond; seats the attestors as the receipt committee from block zero; sets the sudo key and the Root timelock guardian to the multisig accounts the preflight derives, at the runtime's mainnet delays; stores 600-slot sessions, the Cardano mainnet settlement ids, the committee with partner-chain, aura and grandpa keys, and snake_case main-chain scripts; and raises MOTRA generation to 1e10 per MATRA per block. It derives the committee candidate address from the genesis UTXO as partner-chains v1.8.0 does (the v8.1.0 committee candidate validator applied to the UTXO, hashed as Plutus V2) and refuses any other. It refuses, naming the field, a malformed manifest, a key an object names twice, a field or role no reader of the manifest knows, hex that is not 0x, lowercase and two digits a byte of exactly the field's bytes, an output index above 32767, fewer oracles than a price needs or more than a roster holds, development and preprod keys and values, shared keys where sets must be disjoint, non-mainnet Cardano settings, and any role account below its dust floor: the existential deposit, the multisig and recovery deposits its role reserves, and the dust that generates a day of its calls' MOTRA (and, for a role that carries an upgrade, twice a block-long call's fee). Deterministic in manifest order.

primitives.name: Reproducible runtime build
primitives.desc: Builds a commit's runtime blob at a fixed path in a digest-pinned Rust image, with the runtime's build script remapping the toolchain, Cargo home and repository directories its panic messages name, so every builder gets the same bytes and code hash: the code a signed launch manifest pins can be rebuilt from source, and a genesis built from a plain spec carrying it does not depend on the node that ran build-spec.

primitives.name: Root timelock
primitives.desc: Holds every non-exempt Root call for a per-class delay (recovery for committee toggles and delay raises, the standard delay for everything else including consensus-key levers, sudo key rotation and kill-switch restarts unless the guardian co-signs, long for the dedicated bridge and supply levers) in a bounded vetoable queue with a guardian veto, bulk veto, fast-track and a one-shot advance approval that Root runs without a queue place, plus one guardian change the guardian cannot veto and the sudo key can withdraw; the runtime call filter lets the sudo key reach Root at once only for pause, withdrawal and session-bounded finality break-glass calls, for scheduling and for the approved call, each timelock call is charged for every call its classifier walks, and genesis refuses a chain spec without an independent guardian, or with a development account as guardian, and allows an unguarded one only when its sudo key is a development account or absent. Its mainnet delays (DefaultDelays) and their ceiling (MaxDelay) are metadata constants, so a genesis audit can bound the stored delays from the runtime alone. The guardian's veto and co-sign calls (cancel, cancel_all, fast_track, approve), signed by the current guardian directly or through a multisig as_multi wrapper, are given the top transaction-pool priority through the MOTRA fee extension, bounded to one slot per signer and to the wrapped call's own weight, so a stolen sudo key cannot buy its way past the veto and a compromised guardian cannot use the priority to fill blocks. On a chain whose genesis fixed its MATRA issuance the same filter refuses every signed Balances call, vested transfer, billing top-up or withdrawal and attestor bond, however deep a batch, derivative, multisig or recovered account wraps it, while Root's force calls still run after their delay.

primitives.name: Seat-key probe
primitives.desc: Lists the session keys a running validator's keystore names, with no unsafe RPC: finds every process with an authority flag, tells its chain by the database it holds open, refuses dev keys held in memory, and walks to the keystore in the node's own root without following a link. Its named set is an upper bound that never leaves out a key the node can sign with, so it can refuse a seat named on two hosts but never prove a host signs; positive claims come from chain evidence.

primitives.name: Native ZK and hybrid MATRA specification
primitives.desc: Phase-aware PREPROD native ZK acceptance harness with a real Rust driver, namespace-isolated core tests and dependency negative control, source-derived mainnet file-route refusal, actual runtime metadata compatibility and mutants, Aiken codec evaluation and measured no_std Sapling Wasm verification. --full always validates the lock and unit tests, selecting phases through CURRENT_PHASE only for ZK/spec changes against FPL_DIFF_BASE or the origin/main merge-base; --all retains every end-state check regardless of paths. CI filters ZK, spec, harness, runtime, pallet and chain-spec paths; the Sapling spike and independently rebuilt runtime metadata comparison, pinned to partnerchain/Cargo.lock, run only for ZK/spec changes. The required Rust workflow has no P0 baseline gate. Mainnet, spend and external commitments remain denied.

primitives.name: Native ZK bridge recipient codec
primitives.desc: Standalone canonical v1 Account and Utxo CBOR recipient codecs in no_std Rust and Aiken, with actual CEK evaluator round trips and refusal of reserved Shielded, unknown version/tag/lock, malformed length, trailing bytes and noncanonical integers. P0 primitive only; no deployed bridge or value activation.

primitives.name: Native ZK Sapling verification core
primitives.desc: Experimental no_std Sapling verification core using arkworks Groth16/BLS12-381 and upstream Sapling/Jubjub signatures and tree primitives. Rust 1.85.0 wasm32 build, pinned real Zcash mainnet corpus, exhaustive proof-bit mutations and public-input controls that reject a pairing-result bypass and complete one-spend/two-output bundle measurements. Standalone P0 feasibility primitive; no runtime pool, value activation or reviewed slowest-hardware claim.

primitives.name: CI sccache store
primitives.desc: Shared sccache store for the Rust CI on both Woodpecker agents: nginx WebDAV on Node-3 (192.168.0.133:3910, LAN only) over TLS 1.3 under a pinned, name-constrained CA whose key is destroyed, every request authenticated, reads for the reader and writer and every change for the writer alone, with no delete or move. Pull requests build with the reader (the store refuses their writes and client.sh fails a read-only step whose write it takes); only push pipelines on main get the writer, a Woodpecker secret released to push events, and the writer reads nothing (SCCACHE_RECACHE): main compiles every crate and replaces its entry, so no stored entry reaches a main build. Memory 512 MiB, one CPU, least-recently-read eviction from 40 GiB down to 32 GiB; an unanswering store leaves builds uncached.
